decisions.latin: desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum … ita desíderat ánima mea ad te
decisions.why: The Latin says the same verb twice, and the likeness rests on it; both colons keep one Portuguese verb. *desideráre* is to long for (L&S); the Greek ἐπιποθεῖ is to yearn. *desejar* is the plain cognate. The preposition *ad* (ἐπί) is absorbed: *desejar* takes a direct object in Portuguese (grammar, D2). DRB 'panteth after' and MS1932 *suspira por* give the animal's breath, which the Latin verb does not name. *ansiar por* is the concupíscere row's word (118:20) and would merge two Latin verbs.

options.label: anseia pelas … anseia por vós
options.note: keeps *ad* as *por*; *ansiar por* is concupíscere's (118:20), so two Latin verbs would meet in one Portuguese.

options.label: suspira pelas … suspira por vós
options.note: MS1932; DRB 'panteth' — an image the Latin verb does not have.

decisions.why: The cervus row (open) proposes *cervo* wherever the colon itself names the animal's world — and 41:2 is the case it names: the springs of water and the thirst of 41:3. *servo* (homophone in Brazil) was heard at 17:34; here *o cervo deseja as fontes das águas* leaves no room for a servant, since the sentence is about drinking. *veado* (MS1932) is a slur in Brazil.

options.label: o cervo
options.note: Ruling; the row's proposal for this verse; DRB 'hart'.

options.label: a corça
options.note: 17:34, 28:9; no homophone, gender lost. If chosen, *corça* everywhere would make one word for the psalter.

decisions.why: The perfect (ἐδίψησεν). The thirst is plainly still present — the question follows — so the tense is the Hebrew-Greek perfect of a state; DRB keeps it as 'hath thirsted', MS1932 turns it to *tem sede*. Portuguese has no light perfect that says 'has been and still is'. Kept as the Latin's perfect: *teve sede* is not heard as over, because the next colon asks *quando?*

options.label: tem sede
options.note: MS1932; the state, in the present.

decisions.why: Two adjectives without a conjunction (DRB 'the strong living God'). Portuguese cannot stack them after the noun without a link; *e* is supplied, as MS1932 does. (The Easter Vigil tract, missa/Tempora/Quad6-6, reads *ad Deum vivum* without *fortem*; the psalter's reading is followed.)

options.label: forte, do Deus vivo
options.note: no conjunction, but *Deus* supplied a second time.

decisions.why: *veníre* is 'come'; the psalmist is far away (41:7), and Portuguese *vir* points towards the speaker, so *quando virei* is heard as said from the temple. *chegar* is the arrival *veníre* names, from any standpoint; *ir* (MS1932) names the setting out instead. ἥξω is 'I shall arrive'. v2: the stylist asked for *irei* (the colon was +3 and *chegarei, e aparecerei* stumbled); taken.

options.label: irei
options.note: Ruling (v2): stylist and MS1932 — plainer and three syllables shorter; *ir* avoids the wrong standpoint of *vir* as well as *chegar* does.

options.label: chegarei
options.note: draft 1; ἥξω "arrive". The stylist found it weaker and the colon crowded (*chegarei, e aparecerei*).

options.label: virei
options.note: the cognate sense; wrong standpoint in Portuguese.

decisions.why: The Latin's plural (ἄρτος is singular in Rahlfs; the Latin has *panes*) and the dative *mihi*. *os meus pães* is heard as loaves; *pão* is how Portuguese says food (as 40:10 *comia o meu pão*, D29 on number). The dative becomes the possessive: *foram o meu pão* = 'were bread to me'. v2: the Latinist (minor) asked for *os meus pães*; refused as at 40:10 (the idiom; number is grammar, D2, D29). Option 3.

options.label: pão para mim
options.note: the dative kept as a preposition.

decisions.why: *cotídie* here and *per síngulos dies* in 41:11b are one Greek phrase, καθ᾿ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν (Rahlfs, both verses), so by D15's test one Portuguese: the per síngulos dies row's *todos os dias* (7:12). The Easter Vigil tract even reads *per síngulos dies* in this verse (Quad6-6). The two verses then echo each other as the Greek does. *dícitur* impersonal passive → *me dizem* (grammar).

options.label: cada dia
options.note: keeps the Latin's two words apart.

decisions.why: *in me* can be 'within me' (DRB 'in me', MS1932 *dentro de mim mesmo*) or, with the Greek ἐπ᾿ ἐμέ, 'upon / over me' (Augustine's *super me*). *em mim* keeps the Latin's openness; *dentro de mim* closes it. It also keeps 41:5 apart from 41:7 *ad meípsum* → *dentro de mim mesmo*, a different Latin phrase. v2: the blind reader heard it as grief within, being refilled, or poured out to God — the openness the Latin has; kept.

D5 leaves the noun *conféssio* open, to be decided where met. Here it is the ἐξομολόγησις of the festal throng, set beside exultation, and three verses on the verb of the same root is the refrain's *confitébor illi* → *lhe darei graças* (D5). *ação de graças* keeps the family audible inside the psalm. DRB and MS1932 have 'praise' (*louvor*), which is laus's word. v2: the stylist heard *exultação e de ação* as a tongue-twister and asked *louvor*; refused — *louvor* is laus's, and *ação de graças* keeps the noun beside the refrain's *darei graças* (D5). His line is option 2.

options.label: de ação de graças
options.note: Ruling: the noun of D5's verb.

decisions.why: *epulári* is to feast, sit at a banquet (L&S); the Greek ἑορτάζοντος is 'keeping festival'. The Latin's image is the table, and a participle (one who feasts), singular. *sonus → som* (18:5). MS1932 *ruído dum festim* makes the participle a noun.

options.label: o som de quem se banqueteia

forms.epulantis: o som de quem se banqueteia

options.note: Ruling: the participle and the banquet.

options.label: o som de quem está em festa

forms.epulantis: o som de quem está em festa

options.note: the Greek's festival; the table lost.

options.label: o som de um banquete
options.note: MS1932's build (*ruído dum festim*); the person lost.

decisions.why: The refrain (41:6, 41:11b; 42:5 — and 42:5–6 are said at the foot of the altar, missa/Ordo/Ordo.txt). The soul is spoken to as one person, so *tu* (*estás*, *me perturbas*, *Espera*), as MS1932. The vocative takes no article in Portuguese; *minha alma* is the vocative as *meu Deus* is (21:2 *Deus, meu Deus*). The Latin has no *O*. conturbáre → perturbar (row). One decision fills both verses so the refrain cannot drift; Ps 42 should copy it.

options.label: ó minha alma
options.note: the vocative marked, as *ó Deus* for a bare *Deus*.

options.label: alma minha
options.note: the Latin's order; literary in Brazil.

decisions.latin: salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus
decisions.why: The refrain's close (41:6b = 41:12 = 42:6). Two nouns in apposition to *illi* (God), without a verb, as the Latin. salutáre → salvação (D6), vultus → rosto (row; *face* is fácies's). The articles are Portuguese grammar. MS1932 supplies *a ele que é*; the Latin's bare apposition is kept, after a mediant that already names 'him'. Two slots, one decision, so the two verses cannot drift. v2: the blind reader heard it as a title of God, meaning obscure — the Latin image; kept. Ps 42 v2 (42:6) has the same words.

options.label: a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

forms.salutare6: a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus
forms.salutare12: a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

options.label: a ele, salvação do meu rosto e meu Deus

forms.salutare6: a ele, salvação do meu rosto e meu Deus
forms.salutare12: a ele, salvação do meu rosto e meu Deus

options.note: MS1932's build (*a ele que é a salvação…*), without his relative clause.

decisions.latin: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est
decisions.why: πρὸς ἐμαυτόν, 'towards / within myself'; DRB 'within myself', MS1932 *Dentro de mim mesmo*. *-ipsum* → *mesmo*. conturbáta est → *está perturbada*, the state (6:4 *a minha alma está muito perturbada*, the same Greek ἐταράχθη). v2: the stylist found *Dentro de mim mesmo a minha alma* muddy (three m-syllables) and a translated phrase at the head; the verb is put first (order, D2) and *mesmo* kept.

options.label: A minha alma está perturbada dentro de mim mesmo

forms.meipsum: A minha alma está perturbada dentro de mim mesmo

options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's order (*mim mesmo a minha* clotted); *mesmo* for *-ipsum* kept against his *dentro de mim*.

options.label: Dentro de mim mesmo a minha alma está perturbada

forms.meipsum: Dentro de mim mesmo a minha alma está perturbada

options.note: draft 1: the Latin's order; DRB, MS1932.

options.label: A minha alma está perturbada dentro de mim

forms.meipsum: A minha alma está perturbada dentro de mim

options.note: stylist's line; drops *mesmo* (-ipsum) — refused as a lost word.

options.label: Para comigo a minha alma está perturbada

forms.meipsum: Para comigo a minha alma está perturbada

decisions.why: The Latin transliterates the Greek Ερμωνιιμ, itself the Hebrew plural 'the Hermons' (the peaks of Hermon). A Latin reader hears a foreign name, not a plural. *Hermon* is the name a Brazilian ear knows (MS1932). *Hermoniim* (DRB) keeps the Latin's letters; *dos Hermons* translates a plural the Latin does not translate. v2: the stylist asked that *e do Hermon* not hang alone; the comma after *Jordão* is removed, joining it to *terra* (DRB "from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim"). The Latinist (minor) asked for the plural *dos Hermons*; refused — the Latin transliterates a name, it does not translate a plural; his wording is option 3.

invocáre → invocar (row, working). The Latin's verb is the one used of calling on God (ἐπικαλεῖται); the deep calls on the deep. *chamar* (MS1932 *chama outro abismo*) is plainer and flattens it. The repetition *abismo … abismo* is the Latin's and stays; *outro* (MS1932) is not in the Latin.

*excélsa* is 'high things, heights' (DRB 'heights'; 17:34 *super excélsa* → *sobre as alturas*). The Greek μετεωρισμοί are the lifted swells of the sea, and MS1932 reads it so (*vagas amontoadas*). The Latin says heights; kept, with the waves beside it making the sea plain. v2: the blind reader heard heights first and the billows second, and found *passaram sobre mim* odd with heights — the Latin's own strangeness; kept.

The mandáre row is open between *dar ordem* and *mandar*. With a thing as object *dar ordem* cannot stand (*deu ordem à sua misericórdia*), as at 7:7b. *mandar* in Portuguese is both 'command' and 'send', which is exactly the reach of the Latin here (DRB 'commanded', MS1932 *enviou*).

decisions.latin: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ
decisions.why: Verbless in Latin (DRB 'With me is prayer'); the copula is supplied. The apud row gives *junto de* (21:26 *Junto de vós está o meu louvor*); with the first person Portuguese says *comigo*, the plainer of two faithful words (D2). The prayer is what the psalmist has left, by night, with the canticle.

options.label: Dentro de mim está
options.note: MS1932 *Dentro de mim orarei* — his verb is supplied; and *dentro* is 41:7's.

decisions.why: The present passive. v2: the stylist found *são quebrados* flat and asked for the pronominal passive, which keeps the voice and the tense and puts *ossos* at the mediant; taken (grammar, D2).

options.label: são quebrados (os meus ossos são quebrados)
options.note: draft 1; the analytic passive; MS1932 the same.

choices.41:2: quemádmodum … ita → *Assim como … assim* (the comparison; the quemádmodum row). The vocative *Deus* → *ó Deus*, as elsewhere. fons → *fonte*; *as fontes das águas* as 17:16a. Uses: a Mass Gradual (missa/Sancti/06-04), a versicle (04-16 Labre), Hildegard's office.
choices.41:3: apparére → *aparecer* (16:15). *ante fáciem Dei* → *diante da face de Deus* (fácies row). The Easter Vigil tract sings 41:2–4 (missa/Tempora/Quad6-6).
choices.41:4: die ac nocte → *de dia e de noite*. *Ubi est Deus tuus?* → *Onde está o teu Deus?* — the scoffers speak to one man: *tu*. Same words in 41:11b.
choices.41:5: recordári → *lembrar-se de*; *Hæc* (plural) → *destas coisas* (MS1932), put after the verb (order, D2). transíre in → *passar a*; the verb returns in 41:8b (*passaram sobre mim*), as *transíbo … transiérunt*. tabernáculum → *tenda* (row, open; 14:1); admirábilis → *admirável* (row, which names this verse). usque ad → *até*. quóniam → *porque* (the Latin's causal; DRB 'for'). The blind reader heard *tenda* as tent, helped by *casa de Deus*, with the shop sense possible; the row stands.
choices.41:5b: in voce → *com voz de*: the sound that goes with the procession of 41:5. vox → *voz* both here and in 41:8.
choices.41:6: The refrain; 41:11b's second colon and 42:5's are the same words. contúrbas → *perturbas* (conturbáre row).
choices.41:6b: speráre in → *esperar em* (D36); the imperative is *tu* (to the soul). adhuc → *ainda*. confitéri → *dar graças a* (D5), with *lhe* for *illi*. 41:6b = 41:12 = 42:6; it closes the prayers at the foot of the altar (missa/Ordo/Ordo.txt).
choices.41:7: memor ero → *me lembrarei de* (future, as the Latin; MS1932's *me lembrei* is not the Latin's tense). *de terra … a monte* → *desde … desde*. *módicus* → *pequeno*: *módico* in Portuguese is 'modest in price'; the adjective before the noun (order, D2). The blind reader heard *desde* as place first (time second).
choices.41:8: cataráctæ → *cataratas* (the floodgates, as 'as cataratas do céu' of the Flood); *tuárum* → *vossas*.
choices.41:8b: fluctus → *ondas* (new row). *super me transiérunt* → *passaram sobre mim* (natural order).
choices.41:9: In die … nocte → *De dia … de noite* (as 41:4). *cánticum ejus* → *o seu cântico*: 'his' left open as the Latin (the Lord's song, or a song to him — DRB 'to him').
choices.41:9b: suscéptor → *amparo* (D19). *dicam* → *direi*. The words said to God are *vós*; *Vós* named as subject so the short line has its weight. Deus vitæ meæ → *o Deus da minha vida*.
choices.41:10: oblivísci → *esquecer* with a direct object (row; 12:1). *contristátus incédo* → *ando entristecido* — 37:7 *contristátus ingrediébar → andava entristecido*. 42:2 has *tristis incédo* (another adjective) and should say *ando triste*. afflígere → *afligir* (row); *dum* → *enquanto* in all four verses (41:4, 10, 11, 11b). Ps 42 v2 has *e por que ando triste, enquanto me aflige o inimigo?* — the *dum* clause identical.
choices.41:11: confríngere → *quebrar* (row). exprobráre → *afrontar* (row; 34:7, 118:42). tribuláre → *atribular* (row). *qui tríbulant me inimíci mei* in natural order: *os meus inimigos que me atribulam*. The Latin's tenses (present, then perfect) kept.
choices.41:11b: per síngulos dies → *todos os dias* (row, which names this verse). After a question mark inside the verse the next word stays lower-case, as the Latin prints it.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm41.txt, 16 prayed verses (41:2–41:12 with 41:5b, 6b, 8b, 9b, 11b; no 41:1, the titulus, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Uses (ps032/uses.py): 41:2 a Gradual (missa/Sancti/06-04), a versicle (Labre), Hildegard's office; 41:2–4 the Easter Vigil tract (Quad6-6, reading *ad Deum vivum* and *per síngulos dies*); the refrain 42:5–6 (= 41:6, 41:12) in the prayers at the foot of the altar (missa/Ordo). Not in the Diurnal Monástico parallels. Ps 42 (the same psalm in the Hebrew, with the same refrain) is translated in parallel; its folder had only literal.json when this draft was written, so the refrain is proposed here as a formula row for it to copy.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps041.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D5 (confitébor → darei graças; the noun conféssio decided here as *ação de graças*), D6 (salutáre), D19 (suscéptor), D36 (speráre in). Latin readings kept against the Greek: 41:8b *excélsa* as heights. Tests for the readers: *o cervo deseja*, *teve sede*, *chegarei*, *derramei em mim a minha alma*, *a tenda admirável*, *o som de quem se banqueteia*, *minha alma* (vocative), *a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus*, *do Hermon*, *O abismo invoca o abismo*, *as vossas alturas*, *mandou a sua misericórdia*, *Comigo está a oração*.

Draft 1: hard pass. Length: 41:9b first colon +4 (the copula *está* supplied and *Comigo* for *Apud me*), 41:10 second +4 (*entristecido*, 37:7's word), 41:3 second +3, 41:5b second +3 (*quem se banqueteia* for one participle), 41:7 first +3, 41:11 first +3, 41:5 second −3; accepted. Rhyme flags 41:2–5 (-eus): the finals are *Deus* four times, as the Latin's are *Deus … Dei … Deus tuus … Dei* — the echo is the Latin's, accepted. Cadences: oxytone finals on *Deus*, *mim*, allowed by rule 4.
Refrain rows proposed early (formulas, open) so that the Ps 42 agent, working in parallel, can copy them: *Quare tristis es…* and *Spera in Deo…*, with the near-twin 42:2 noted.
codex.py not called (Codex out of credits since Ps 37; AGENT-BRIEF step 5). Latinist, stylist and ambiguity readers for draft 1 handed to the coordinator.

Draft 1, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context; Codex out of credits). No major; two minors, both on number. «A close, faithful rendering: tenses, persons and the Latin's images are preserved, and the pointing marks match the Latin throughout.» Both refused.

outcomes.reason: *comer / ter por pão* is the Portuguese idiom; *os meus pães* is heard as loaves; number is grammar (D2, D29), as 40:10. Option 3.
The Latin transliterates a name (Ερμωνιιμ); it does not translate a plural, and a Latin reader hears a name. *dos Hermons* is option 3, *de Hermoniim* option 2.

audit.note: Rows added (open): epulári, abýssus / cataráctæ, fluctus, excélsa (noun), sitíre ad, panes (lácrimæ panes), módicus, contristári / incédere, effúndere ánimam in me, ad meípsum, apud me (first person), Hermóniim; formula row *Abýssus abýssum ínvocat*. Evidence added to confríngere, oppróbrium / exprobráre, tabernáculum, lácrimæ / fletus, oblivísci (the -eris row), tribuláre, conturbáre, exsultáre, invocáre, mandáre, confitéri (the noun), and the two refrain rows. Refrain (41:6, 6b, 11b, 12) and 41:10 unchanged since v1 and identical with ps042 (42:5 second colon, 42:6, 42:2's *dum* clause).
